chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ar-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Amiri from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The earth does not cease to have an authority (Hujjah) from Allah in it, who knows the permissible and the impermissible, and invites people to the way of Allah.

key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: Authority or proof of God, referring to the Imam
key_terms.يَعْرِفُ: He knows, indicating specific divine knowledge

ai.seo_question: Who is the Hujjah of Allah on earth and what are his qualities?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of *Istidrar al-Hujjah*, affirming that God never leaves the earth without a living proof (*Hujjah*) who serves as the definitive interpreter of divine law. By emphasizing the Hujjah's role in distinguishing halal from haram and guiding humanity, it reinforces the necessity of continuous, infallible leadership (*Imamah*) as the conduit for spiritual and legal authority. This concept is foundational to understanding the transition from the Prophet to the Imams and ultimately to the Hidden Imam.
